question: SDLC scenario: A clinic permits appointment rescheduling but has no agreed response when the new slot is already taken. What should QA clarify?

question: SDLC scenario: A telecom release note says build D is installed, but the deployment record identifies build C. What should QA reconcile before accepting the attached test evidence?

Assume build C and build D have identical behavior

question: SDLC scenario: A bank design allows a timeout path to submit the same transfer again, while the requirement permits only one transfer per request ID. What should design review address?

Use attendance totals as the sole effectiveness measure
Count all review meetings without examining their content

question: SDLC scenario: An insurer adds a rule effective next month. The current-month behavior must stay unchanged. What should QA distinguish when updating maintained tests?
choices: Apply next month’s rule to all historical dates
Keep only current-month checks and omit the effective-date transition
Treat every difference from the old rule as a defect

question: SDLC scenario: Travel customers ask for instant cancellation, but the agreed process requires an external approval first. How should the team use the feedback?

question: SDLC scenario: A shipping component passes checks with a mock that always returns an address. The approved interface also permits a no-match response. What is the gap?
choices: Rerun only the always-successful mock cases
Verification of the agreed no-match contract and the consumer’s resulting behavior

question: SDLC scenario: A retailer updates a shared eligibility rule. A background renewal job uses the rule without displaying the new screen. Why should impact analysis include that job?
choices: Its business result depends on the changed rule even though its UI did not change
Limit analysis to newly edited screens
Infer every consumer passes from the interactive screen result

question: SDLC scenario: A utility has six days before a fixed review. Full scope needs four implementation days followed by three required test days; reduced scope needs three plus three. Which commitment respects the constraints?

Assume the dependent test phase can finish before implementation
Keep full scope because four implementation days fit the deadline
